claims.text: Malpractice: a successful lawsuit requires proof that care was below the ordinary standard of care that similar health care professionals would provide under similar circumstances, that a professional relationship existed with the injured party, and that the patient was harmed because of the deviation from the standard of care.
claims.quote: successful medical malpractice lawsuits require proof of the following: The care provided was below the ordinary standard of care that would be provided by similar health care professionals under similar circumstances. A professional relationship existed between the health care professional and the injured party. The patient was harmed because of the deviation from the standard of care.

claims.text: Defensive medicine: ordering tests that are not clearly medically necessary to avoid lawsuits exposes patients to risks and expenses not justified by the medical benefit; it is not required by law, may not protect against lawsuits, and is generally considered excessive and inappropriate.
claims.quote: physicians may order tests that are not clearly medically necessary to avoid even a remote possibility of missing something and thus leaving themselves open to a lawsuit. This approach, referred to as defensive medicine, exposes patients to risks (eg, ionizing radiation, need for invasive and/or uncomfortable tests to confirm false-positive results) and expenses that are not justified by the medical benefit. However, such an approach is not required by law, may not protect against lawsuits, and is generally considered excessive and inappropriate.

claims.text: Best defense: providing excellent health care and building close, trusting, collaborative relationships with patients.
claims.quote: The best defense against malpractice lawsuits is providing excellent health care and building close, trusting, collaborative relationships with patients.

claims.text: Licensing: in the United States, all health care professionals must have a state license to practice, and patients can complain to the state licensing board instead of or in addition to bringing a lawsuit.
claims.quote: In the United States, all health care professionals (eg, physicians, nurses, pharmacists) must have a state license to practice their profession. When patients feel that their rights have been violated, they can complain to the state licensing board, instead of or in addition to bringing a lawsuit.

claims.text: Board discipline: if warranted, reprimand, fine, license suspension or license revocation.
claims.quote: If warranted, the board can impose a range of disciplinary actions, including reprimand, fine, license suspension, or license revocation.
